$v_{\min} = \sqrt{rg\,\dfrac{\sin\theta - \mu_s\cos\theta}{\cos\theta + \mu_s\sin\theta}} =$ **{vmin:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Pendulum in an accelerating car
drills.prompt: A {mb} kg ball hangs on a string from the roof of a car that accelerates forward at a steady {acc} m/s². Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the angle of the string from the vertical (in degrees) and the tension in it. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
In the car's frame the ball is at rest under its weight $mg$ (down), the fictitious force $mA$ (backward) and the tension. So $T\cos\theta = mg$ and $T\sin\theta = mA$.

Dividing: $\tan\theta = A/g = {acc}/9.8$, so $\theta =$ **{ang:sig3}°**, tilted backward.

$T = m\sqrt{g^2 + A^2} = {mb}\sqrt{9.8^2 + {acc}^2} =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Artificial gravity in a rotating station
drills.prompt: A ring-shaped space station of radius {r} m spins so that people standing on the rim feel {frac} times Earth's gravity ($g = 9.8$ m/s²). Find its angular speed, its rotation period and its rotation rate in rpm. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The rim must have centripetal acceleration $\omega^2 r = {frac}(9.8) = {geff:num4}$ m/s², so $\omega = \sqrt{{geff:num4}/{r}} =$ **{w:sig3} rad/s**.

Period: $2\pi/\omega =$ **{P:sig3} s**. Rate: $60/{P:num4}$ revolutions per minute $=$ **{rpm:sig3} rpm**.

drills.title: Rocket thrust and liftoff acceleration
drills.prompt: A {mt} t rocket ($1\text{ t} = 1000$ kg) burns {R} kg of propellant per second with an exhaust speed of {ux} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s² and ignoring the nozzle pressure term, find the thrust (N) and the upward acceleration at liftoff (m/s²), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Thrust: $T = uR = ({ux})({R}) =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

Weight: $mg = ({m:dp0})(9.8) = {W:sig4}$ N.

$a = \dfrac{T - mg}{m} =$ **{acc:sig3} m/s²** upward.

drills.title: The rocket equation
drills.prompt: A spacecraft far from any planet has an initial mass of {m0:dp0} kg, of which {pct}% is propellant. Its engine's exhaust speed is {ux} m/s. After it burns all the propellant, what is its mass ratio $m_0/m_f$, and how much speed has it gained? Give both to 3 significant figures (speed in m/s).
drills.solution:
Final mass: $m_f = {m0:dp0}(1 - {pct}/100) = {mf:sig4}$ kg, so the mass ratio is $m_0/m_f =$ **{ratio:sig3}**.

Rocket equation: $\Delta v = u\ln(m_0/m_f) = {ux}\ln({ratio:num4}) =$ **{dv:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Sand falling onto a conveyor belt
drills.prompt: Sand falls straight down onto a conveyor belt at {R} kg/s. The belt moves at a steady {v} m/s. Find the extra force the motor must supply (N), the extra power it delivers (W), and the rate at which heat is produced (W). Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Each second {R} kg of sand gains horizontal momentum ${R}({v})$, so $F = Rv =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

$P = Fv = Rv^2 =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

Kinetic energy given to the sand per second: $\tfrac12Rv^2 = {Q:sig4}$ W. The rest is heat: ${P:sig4} - {Q:sig4} =$ **{Q:sig3} W**, exactly half the power.

drills.title: Head-on collision with a coefficient of restitution
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg cart moving at {v1} m/s collides head-on with a {m2} kg cart moving at {v2} m/s (negative means the opposite direction). The coefficient of restitution is {cr}. Find both final velocities in m/s to 2 decimal places (positive = the first cart's original direction), and the kinetic energy lost in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Momentum: ${m1}v_{1f} + {m2}v_{2f} = {m1}({v1}) + {m2}({v2}) = {p:num4}$.

Restitution: $v_{2f} - v_{1f} = {cr}\,({v1} - ({v2}))$.

Solving together: $v_{1f} =$ **{v1f:num2} m/s** and $v_{2f} =$ **{v2f:num2} m/s**.

Energy lost: $\mu = \dfrac{({m1})({m2})}{{M}} = {mu:num4}$ kg, $K_{\text{rel}} = \tfrac12\mu(v_{1i} - v_{2i})^2 = {Krel:sig4}$ J, and $K_{\text{lost}} = (1 - {cr}^2)K_{\text{rel}} =$ **{Kloss:sig3} J**.

drills.title: A bouncing ball
drills.prompt: A ball is dropped from {h0} m onto a hard floor. The coefficient of restitution is {cr}. Ignoring air resistance, how high does it rise after bounce number {n}, and what total distance does it travel before it stops? Give both in meters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Each bounce reaches $e^2 = {cr}^2$ times the previous height, so after {n} bounces $h = {h0}({cr})^{2 \times {n}} =$ **{hn:sig3} m**.

Total distance: $D = h_0\dfrac{1 + e^2}{1 - e^2} = {h0}\cdot\dfrac{1 + {cr}^2}{1 - {cr}^2} =$ **{D:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Friction needed for rolling down a slope
drills.prompt: A {M} kg {shape} rolls without slipping down a slope at {th}° to the horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its acceleration (m/s²), the static friction force on it (N), and the smallest coefficient of static friction that allows rolling without slipping, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
With $I_{\text{cm}} = cMR^2$ and $c = {shape:num1}$: along the slope $Mg\sin\theta - f = Ma$; about the center $fR = cMR^2(a/R)$, so $f = cMa$.

$a = \dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1 + c} = \dfrac{9.8\sin {th}^\circ}{1 + {shape:num1}} =$ **{acc:sig3} m/s²**.

$f = cMa = {shape:num1}({M})({acc:num3}) =$ **{fr:sig3} N**.

$\mu_s \ge \dfrac{c}{1 + c}\tan\theta =$ **{mu:sig3}**.

drills.title: From skidding to rolling
drills.prompt: A bowling ball (a uniform solid sphere) is released on a level lane at {v0} m/s with no spin. The coefficient of kinetic friction is {mu}. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find how long it skids (s), how far it travels while skidding (m), and its speed once it rolls without slipping (m/s), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Kinetic friction slows the center, $v = v_0 - \mu_kgt$, and spins the ball up, $R\omega = \tfrac52\mu_kgt$. Rolling starts when they are equal:

$t_1 = \dfrac{2v_0}{7\mu_kg} = \dfrac{2({v0})}{7({mu})(9.8)} =$ **{t1:sig3} s**.

Distance: $v_0t_1 - \tfrac12\mu_kgt_1^2 =$ **{d:sig3} m**.

Speed: $v_1 = \tfrac57v_0 =$ **{v1:sig3} m/s** (also from conservation of angular momentum about a point on the lane).

drills.title: Gyroscope precession rate
drills.prompt: A bicycle wheel of mass {M} kg and radius {R} m (treat it as a thin hoop) spins at {rps} rev/s. Its axle is horizontal and supported at one end, with the wheel's center {r} m from the support. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the precession angular speed (rad/s) and the time for one trip around the support (s), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$I = MR^2 = {I:num4}$ kg·m²; $\omega = 2\pi({rps}) = {w:num2}$ rad/s; torque $\tau = Mgr = {tau:num3}$ N·m.

$\Omega = \dfrac{\tau}{I\omega} =$ **{Om:sig3} rad/s**; one trip takes $2\pi/\Omega =$ **{Tp:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Forces in an A-frame truss
drills.prompt: Two rafters meet at the peak of a symmetric A-frame, each at {th}° to the horizontal, with a horizontal tie joining their feet. The walls push straight up at the feet. A {P} kN load acts at the peak. Find the compression in each rafter and the tension in the tie, in kN to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Peak joint: $2F\sin\theta = P$, so $F = \dfrac{{P}}{2\sin {th}^\circ} =$ **{F:sig3} kN**.

Foot joint: the tie balances the rafter's horizontal push, $T = F\cos\theta =$ **{T:sig3} kN**.

drills.title: Ladder against a smooth wall
drills.prompt: A uniform {m} kg ladder leans against a smooth wall at {th}° above the floor. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the friction force the floor must supply (N). Then, if $\mu_s = {mu}$ at the floor, find the smallest angle at which the ladder can stand (degrees). Give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about the foot: $N_wL\sin\theta = W\tfrac L2\cos\theta$, and $f = N_w$, so $f = W/(2\tan\theta) = \dfrac{{W:num1}}{2\tan {th}^\circ} =$ **{f:sig3} N**.

Slipping starts when $f = \mu_sW$: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{2\mu_s} = \dfrac{1}{2({mu})}$, so $\theta_{\min} =$ **{thmin:sig3}°**.

drills.title: Tip or slide when pushed
drills.prompt: A uniform box of mass {m} kg is {w} m deep in the direction you push. You push horizontally at a height of {H} m; $\mu_s = {mu}$ with the floor. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the force needed to start it sliding (N), the force needed to start it tipping (N), and the push height above which it tips before it slides (m), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Sliding: $F = \mu_smg =$ **{Fs:sig3} N**.

Tipping about the bottom edge on the far side from you: $FH = mg\tfrac w2$, so $F = \dfrac{mgw}{2H} =$ **{Ft:sig3} N**. Whichever force is smaller happens first.

Equal when $w/(2H) = \mu_s$: $H = w/(2\mu_s) =$ **{Hc:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Speeds on an elliptical orbit
drills.prompt: A satellite's orbit has its perigee {hp} km and its apogee {ha} km above Earth's surface. Using $R_E = 6.37\times10^6$ m and $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find its speed at perigee and at apogee (km/s) and its period (hours), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Distances from Earth's center: $r_p = {rp:texsci}$ m, $r_a = {ra:texsci}$ m, so $a = \tfrac12(r_p + r_a) = {a:texsci}$ m.

Vis-viva: $v_p = \sqrt{GM\left(\dfrac2{r_p} - \dfrac1a\right)} =$ **{vp:sig3} km/s**.

Angular momentum: $v_a = v_p\dfrac{r_p}{r_a} =$ **{va:sig3} km/s**.

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{a^3/GM} =$ **{T:sig3} h**.

drills.title: Hohmann transfer between circular orbits
drills.prompt: A spacecraft moves by Hohmann transfer from a circular orbit {h1} km above Earth's surface to a circular orbit {h2} km up. Using $R_E = 6.37\times10^6$ m and $GM_E = 3.98\times10^{14}$ m³/s², find the first and second burns (km/s) and the transfer time (hours), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Radii: $r_1 = {r1:texsci}$ m, $r_2 = {r2:texsci}$ m; transfer orbit $a_t = \tfrac12(r_1 + r_2) = {at:texsci}$ m.

Circular speeds: $v_1 = \sqrt{GM/r_1} = {v1:dp0}$ m/s, $v_2 = \sqrt{GM/r_2} = {v2:dp0}$ m/s.

Vis-viva on the transfer orbit: ${vtp:dp0}$ m/s at periapsis, ${vta:dp0}$ m/s at apoapsis.

First burn $= {vtp:dp0} - {v1:dp0}$ m/s $=$ **{dv1:sig3} km/s**; second burn $= {v2:dp0} - {vta:dp0}$ m/s $=$ **{dv2:sig3} km/s**.

Transfer time: half the transfer period, $\pi\sqrt{a_t^3/GM} =$ **{tt:sig3} h**.

drills.title: Mass of a planet from a moon's orbit
drills.prompt: A small moon orbits a planet with semimajor axis ${am}\times10^{{ae}}$ m and period {Td} days. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², find the planet's mass in kg, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Convert the period: $T = {Td}(86\,400) = {Ts:texsci}$ s.

$M = \dfrac{4\pi^2a^3}{GT^2} = \dfrac{4\pi^2({am}\times10^{{ae}})^3}{(6.67\times10^{-11})({Ts:texsci})^2} = \mathbf{{M:texsci}}$ kg.

drills.title: Decay of a lightly damped oscillator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block on a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m is damped by a force $-bv$ with $b = {b:dp2}$ kg/s. Find the quality factor $Q$, the time for the amplitude to fall to half, and how many oscillations that takes. Give each to 3 significant figures (treat the period as the undamped period).
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {w0:num4}$ rad/s, so $Q = \dfrac{m\omega_0}{\,b} = \dfrac{\sqrt{mk}}{\,b} =$ **{Q:sig3}**.

The amplitude goes as $e^{-bt/(2m)}$; setting it to $\tfrac12$ gives $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{2m\ln 2}{\,b} = \dfrac{2({m})(0.6931)}{{b:dp2}} =$ **{th:sig3} s**.

The period is $2\pi/\omega_0 = {T0:num4}$ s, so that's $t_{1/2}/T =$ **{ncyc:sig3}** oscillations.

drills.title: Amplitude of a driven, damped oscillator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m has damping constant $b = {b:num1}$ kg/s. It is driven by a force $F_0\cos(\omega t)$ with $F_0 = {F0:num1}$ N and $\omega = {w:dp0}$ rad/s. Find the static stretch $F_0/k$ and the steady-state amplitude, both in mm to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {wn}$ rad/s and $Q = m\omega_0/b = {Q:num2}$. The static stretch is $F_0/k =$ **{stat:sig3} mm**.

$A = \dfrac{F_0/m}{\sqrt{(\omega_0^2 - \omega^2)^2 + (b\omega/m)^2}}$ with $\omega_0^2 - \omega^2 = {wn}^2 - {w:dp0}^2$ gives **{A:sig3} mm**. (At $\omega = \omega_0$ this is $Q$ times the static stretch.)

drills.title: Critical damping
drills.prompt: A machine of mass {m:dp0} kg sits on mounts with total spring constant $k = {kk:dp0}\,000$ N/m. Find its natural frequency $f_0$ (Hz) and the damping constant (kg/s) that would make it critically damped, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {w0:num4}$ rad/s, so $f_0 = \omega_0/2\pi =$ **{f0:sig3} Hz**.

$b_c = 2\sqrt{mk} = 2m\omega_0 =$ **{bc:sig3} kg/s**. (With, say, $b = {frac:num2}\,b_c$ instead, $Q = \sqrt{mk}/b = {Q:num2}$: underdamped, so it would overshoot before settling.)

drills.title: Equal-tempered note frequencies
drills.prompt: In equal temperament with A4 = 440 Hz, what is the frequency of the note {n} semitones {dir} A4? Give it in Hz to the nearest 0.1 Hz.
drills.solution:
Each semitone multiplies the frequency by $2^{1/12}$, so $f = 440 \cdot 2^{\pm n/12}$ with the minus sign for notes below.

$2^{{ex}/12} = {ratio:num4}$, so $f = 440 \times {ratio:num4} =$ **{freq:num1} Hz**.

drills.title: Pitch difference in cents
drills.prompt: How many cents higher is a {f2} Hz tone than a {f1} Hz tone? Give the answer to the nearest cent.
drills.solution: cents $= 1200\log_2\dfrac{f_2}{f_1} = 1200\log_2\dfrac{{f2}}{{f1}} = 1200 \times \dfrac{\ln({f2}/{f1})}{\ln 2} =$ **{c:num1} cents**, about {semis:num2} equal-tempered semitones.

drills.title: Beats between harmonics of a mistuned interval
drills.prompt: A note of {f1} Hz is played with a second note meant to be a pure {iv} above it, but the second note is actually {f2:num1} Hz. Which harmonics nearly coincide, and at what rate do they beat? Give the beat frequency in Hz to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution:
A pure ratio of {a}:{bb} would put the upper note at {pure:num1} Hz, and then harmonic {a} of the lower note equals harmonic {bb} of the upper.

Harmonic {a} of {f1} Hz: {h1:num1} Hz. Harmonic {bb} of {f2:num1} Hz: {h2:num1} Hz. Beat frequency $= |{h1:num1} - {h2:num1}| =$ **{fb:num1} Hz**.

drills.title: Reflection at an acoustic boundary
drills.prompt: Ultrasound passes straight on from a tissue with density {rho1:dp0} kg/m³ and sound speed {v1:dp0} m/s into one with density {rho2:dp0} kg/m³ and sound speed {v2:dp0} m/s. What percentage of the intensity is reflected, and what percentage is transmitted? Give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$Z_1 = \rho_1 v_1 = {z1:num4}\times10^6$ and $Z_2 = \rho_2 v_2 = {z2:num4}\times10^6$ kg/(m²·s).

$R = \left(\dfrac{Z_2 - Z_1}{Z_2 + Z_1}\right)^2 =$ **{R:sig3}%**, and $T = 100\% - R =$ **{T:sig3}%**.

drills.title: Echo depth and wavelength in ultrasound
drills.prompt: A {fmhz:num1} MHz ultrasound pulse returns an echo {tus} μs after it was sent. Using $v = 1540$ m/s, find the depth of the reflecting boundary (cm) and the wavelength in tissue (mm), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The echo makes a round trip, so $d = \dfrac{vt}{2} = \dfrac{1540 \times {tus}\times10^{-6}}{2} =$ **{dcm:sig3} cm**.

$\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{1540}{{fmhz:num1}\times10^6} =$ **{lmm:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Doppler ultrasound of blood flow
drills.prompt: A {fmhz:num1} MHz ultrasound beam makes an angle of {th}° with blood flowing toward the probe at {u:num2} m/s. Using $\Delta f = 2fu\cos\theta/v$ with $v = 1540$ m/s, find the Doppler shift in Hz to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\Delta f = \dfrac{2fu\cos\theta}{v} = \dfrac{2({fmhz:num1}\times10^6)({u:num2})\cos {th}^\circ}{1540} =$ **{df:sig3} Hz**.

drills.title: Pressure to push liquid through a needle
drills.prompt: Laminar flow of {eta} passes at {Qml} mL/s through a needle {Lcm} cm long with an inner radius of {Rmm} mm. Use Poiseuille's law to find the pressure difference between the ends of the needle, in pascals to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Convert to SI: $R = {rad:texsci}$ m, $L = {len}$ m, $Q = {qsi:texsci}$ m³/s.

Flow resistance: $R_{\text{flow}} = \dfrac{8\eta L}{\pi R^4} = \dfrac{8({eta})({len})}{\pi({rad:texsci})^4} = {Rf:texsci}$ Pa·s/m³.

$\Delta P = QR_{\text{flow}} =$ **{dP:sig3} Pa**.

drills.title: Terminal speed of a small droplet
drills.prompt: A water droplet (density 1000 kg/m³) of radius {rum} µm falls through still air (density 1.2 kg/m³, viscosity $1.8\times10^{-5}$ Pa·s). Using Stokes's law and $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its terminal speed in mm/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v_T = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho_s - \rho_f)g}{9\eta} = \dfrac{2({rad:texsci})^2(1000 - 1.2)(9.8)}{9(1.8\times10^{-5})} = {vt:texsci}$ m/s $=$ **{vmm:sig3} mm/s**.

Tiny droplets settle slowly because $v_T \propto r^2$.

drills.title: Capillary rise

choices.label: water (surface tension 0.073 N/m, density 1000 kg/m³, contact angle 0°)
ethanol (surface tension 0.022 N/m, density 789 kg/m³, contact angle 0°)
mercury (surface tension 0.49 N/m, density 13 600 kg/m³, contact angle 140°)

drills.prompt: A clean glass tube of inner radius {rmm} mm stands in {liq}. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find how far the liquid inside the tube rises above the outside level, in centimeters to 3 significant figures (a negative answer means it sits below the outside level).
drills.solution: $h = \dfrac{2\gamma\cos\theta}{\rho gr} = \dfrac{2({gam})\cos({th}^\circ)}{({dens})(9.8)({rad:texsci})} = {hm:texsci}$ m $=$ **{hcm:sig3} cm**.

drills.title: Efficiency of a rectangular cycle
drills.prompt: A monatomic ideal gas runs the cycle A → B → C → D → A, where A is ({P1} kPa, {V1} L), B is ({P2} kPa, {V1} L), C is ({P2} kPa, {V2} L) and D is ({P1} kPa, {V2} L). Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (J) and the efficiency (%), both to 3 significant figures. (1 kPa·L = 1 J.)
drills.solution:
Net work = enclosed rectangle: $({P2} - {P1})\text{ kPa} \times ({V2} - {V1})\text{ L} =$ **{Wn:sig3} J**.

Heat in: A → B (constant volume) $Q = \tfrac32V\Delta P = 1.5({V1})({P2} - {P1}) = {QAB:sig4}$ J; B → C (constant pressure) $Q = \tfrac52P\Delta V = 2.5({P2})({V2} - {V1}) = {QBC:sig4}$ J. The other two steps give out heat. $Q_{\text{in}} = {Qin:sig4}$ J.

$e = W_{\text{net}}/Q_{\text{in}} =$ **{eff:sig3}%**.

drills.title: Ideal Otto cycle
drills.prompt: An ideal Otto cycle has compression ratio {cr} and uses air ($\gamma = 1.4$) that enters at {T1} K. Find the ideal efficiency (%) and the temperature at the end of the compression stroke (K), both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$e = 1 - \dfrac{1}{r^{\gamma - 1}} = 1 - {cr}^{-0.4} =$ **{eff:sig3}%**.

Adiabatic compression: $T_2 = T_1r^{\gamma - 1} = {T1}({cr})^{0.4} =$ **{T2:sig3} K**.

drills.title: Heat loss through a layered wall
drills.prompt: A wall of area {area} m² has {tins} cm of {kins} and {tw} cm of wood ($k = 0.12$ W/(m·K)). Inside is {Tin}°C and outside {Tout}°C. Find the total thermal resistance per unit area (m²·K/W) and the rate of heat flow through the wall (W), both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$R = L/k$ for each layer: insulation ${R1:sig4}$, wood ${R2:sig4}$; total **{Rt:sig3} m²·K/W**.

$\dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{A\,\Delta T}{R_{\text{total}}} = \dfrac{({area})({dT})}{{Rt:sig4}} =$ **{Pw:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Net radiated power
drills.prompt: A surface of area {area} m² and emissivity {em} is at {TC}°C in surroundings at {TsC}°C. Using $\sigma = 5.67\times10^{-8}$ W/(m²·K⁴), find the net power it loses by radiation, in watts to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Kelvins: $T = {TK}$ K, $T_s = {TsK}$ K.

$P_{\text{net}} = e\sigma A(T^4 - T_s^4) = ({em})(5.67\times10^{-8})({area})({TK}^4 - {TsK}^4) =$ **{Pn:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Equilibrium temperature of a planet
drills.prompt: A planet orbits a Sun-like star at {dau} times Earth's distance and has an albedo of {alb}. The solar constant at Earth is 1361 W/m², and $\sigma = 5.67\times10^{-8}$ W/(m²·K⁴). Find the solar intensity at the planet (W/m²) and its equilibrium temperature (K), both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Inverse square: $S = 1361/{dau}^2 =$ **{S:sig3} W/m²**.

$T_e = \left[\dfrac{(1 - {alb})S}{4\sigma}\right]^{1/4} = \left[\dfrac{(1 - {alb})({S:sig4})}{4(5.67\times10^{-8})}\right]^{1/4} =$ **{Te:sig3} K**.

drills.title: Dipole in a uniform field
drills.prompt: Charges of $\pm{q}$ nC are {dmm} mm apart in a uniform field of {EkN} kN/C, with the dipole moment at ${th}^\circ$ to the field. Find the dipole moment, the magnitude of the torque, and the potential energy $U = -pE\cos\theta$ (signed), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$p = qd = ({q}\times10^{-9})({dmm}\times10^{-3}) = \mathbf{{p:texsci}}$ C·m.

$\tau = pE\sin\theta = ({p:texsci})({E:dp0})\sin{th}^\circ = \mathbf{{tau:texsci}}$ N·m.

$U = -pE\cos\theta = -({p:texsci})({E:dp0})\cos{th}^\circ = \mathbf{{U:texsci}}$ J. (Negative when the moment points within $90^\circ$ of the field, positive beyond.)

drills.title: Field on a dipole's axis
drills.prompt: A dipole is made of $\pm{q}$ nC charges {dmm} mm apart. Find the field on its axis {rcm} cm from its center (a) exactly, from the two point charges, and (b) with the far-field formula $E \approx 2kp/r^3$. Give both in N/C to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
(a) The nearer charge is $r - d/2$ away and the farther one $r + d/2$; their fields point opposite ways along the axis:
$E = kq\left[\dfrac1{(r - d/2)^2} - \dfrac1{(r + d/2)^2}\right] =$ **{Eex:sig3} N/C**.

(b) $p = qd = {p:texsci}$ C·m, so $E \approx \dfrac{2kp}{r^3} =$ **{Eap:sig3} N/C**. The closer $r$ is to $d$, the more the two answers differ.

drills.title: Charge on a balanced oil drop
drills.prompt: An oil drop of mass ${m}\times10^{-15}$ kg hangs motionless between horizontal plates {dmm} mm apart when the voltage across them is {Vr} V. Find the drop's charge (magnitude, in C to 3 significant figures) and the number of excess electrons it carries. ($g = 9.8$ m/s², $e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C)
drills.solution:
Balanced: $qE = mg$ with $E = V/d$, so $q = \dfrac{mgd}{V} = \dfrac{({m}\times10^{-15})(9.8)({dmm}\times10^{-3})}{{Vr}} = \mathbf{{q:texsci}}$ C.

$n = q/e = {q:texsci}/(1.602\times10^{-19}) \approx$ **{n}** electrons.

drills.title: Oil drop radius and mass from its fall
drills.prompt: With the field off, an oil drop (density 900 kg/m³) falls {dist:num2} mm at constant speed in {t:num1} s through air ($\eta = 1.8\times10^{-5}$ Pa·s). Using Stokes's law, find its radius in micrometers and its mass in kg, to 3 significant figures. ($g = 9.8$ m/s²)
drills.solution:
Terminal speed: $v = \dfrac{{dist:num2}\times10^{-3}\text{ m}}{{t:num1}\text{ s}} = {v:texsci}$ m/s.

Drag balances weight, $6\pi\eta rv = \tfrac43\pi r^3\rho g$, so $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{9\eta v}{2\rho g}} = {r:texsci}$ m $=$ **{rum:sig3} μm**.

$m = \tfrac43\pi r^3\rho = \mathbf{{m:texsci}}$ kg.

drills.title: Highest voltage on a charged sphere
drills.prompt: A conducting sphere of radius {Rcm} cm is surrounded by air that breaks down at ${Emax}\times10^6$ V/m. Find the highest potential it can reach (in kV) and the charge it then holds (in μC), to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
At the surface $E = V/R$, so $V_{\max} = E_{\max}R = ({Emax}\times10^6)({R}) =$ **{VkV:sig3} kV**.

$Q = \dfrac{V_{\max}R}{k} = \dfrac{E_{\max}R^2}{k} =$ **{QuC:sig3} μC**.

drills.title: Charge sharing between connected spheres
drills.prompt: Two conducting spheres, of radius {R1} cm and {R2} cm, are far apart and joined by a thin wire. Together they hold {Q} nC. Find the charge on each sphere (nC) and the ratio of the small sphere's surface field to the large sphere's, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Same potential: $kQ_1/R_1 = kQ_2/R_2$, so charge is shared in proportion to radius.

$Q_1 = {Q}\cdot\dfrac{{R1}}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Q1:sig3} nC**, $Q_2 = {Q}\cdot\dfrac{{R2}}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Q2:sig3} nC**.

Surface field $E = V/R$ with the same $V$, so $E_{\text{small}}/E_{\text{large}} = R_1/R_2 =$ **{ratio:sig3}**.

drills.title: Capacitor circuit just after and long after
drills.prompt: An ideal {Ev} V battery, a switch and a resistor $R_1 = {R1}$ kΩ are in series with a parallel pair: a resistor $R_2 = {R2}$ kΩ and an uncharged {C} μF capacitor. Find the battery current (mA) just after the switch closes, the battery current (mA) long after, and the final charge on the capacitor (μC), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Just after: the uncharged capacitor acts as a wire and shorts out $R_2$, so $I = \dfrac{{Ev}\text{ V}}{{R1}\text{ k}\Omega} =$ **{I0:sig3} mA**.

Long after: the charged capacitor acts as a break, so $R_1$ and $R_2$ are in series: $I = \dfrac{{Ev}}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{If:sig3} mA**.

The capacitor has the same voltage as $R_2$: $V_C = I R_2 = {VC:sig3}$ V, so $Q = CV_C = ({C}\ \mu\text{F})({VC:sig3}\text{ V}) =$ **{Q:sig3} μC**.

drills.title: Balanced Wheatstone bridge
drills.prompt: In a Wheatstone bridge, $R_1 = {R1}$ Ω and $R_2 = {R2}$ Ω form one side, and the adjustable $R_3$ and the unknown $R_x$ form the other ($R_1$ and $R_3$ meet at the top corner). The galvanometer reads zero when $R_3 = {R3}$ Ω. Find $R_x$ in ohms, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
At balance P and Q are at the same potential, so both sides divide the voltage in the same ratio: $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{R_3}{R_x}$.

$R_x = \dfrac{R_2R_3}{R_1} = \dfrac{({R2})({R3})}{{R1}} =$ **{Rx:sig3} Ω**.

drills.title: Thévenin equivalent of a loaded divider
drills.prompt: An ideal {Ev} V battery drives a voltage divider: $R_1 = {R1}$ kΩ on top and $R_2 = {R2}$ kΩ below, with terminals across $R_2$. Find the Thévenin voltage (V) and resistance (kΩ) at the terminals, and the voltage (V) across a {RL} kΩ load connected to them. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Open-circuit voltage (the unloaded divider): $V_{\text{th}} = {Ev}\cdot\dfrac{{R2}}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Vth:sig3} V**.

Replace the battery with a wire: $R_1$ and $R_2$ are then in parallel between the terminals, $R_{\text{th}} = \dfrac{({R1})({R2})}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Rth:sig3} kΩ**.

With the load: $I = \dfrac{V_{\text{th}}}{R_{\text{th}} + R_L} = {IL:sig3}$ mA, so $V_L = IR_L =$ **{VL:sig3} V**.

drills.title: Voltmeter loading error
drills.prompt: Resistors $R_1 = {R1}$ MΩ and $R_2 = {R2}$ MΩ are in series across an ideal {Ev} V battery. A voltmeter with resistance {RV} MΩ is connected across $R_2$. Find the true voltage across $R_2$ with no meter attached (V), the meter's reading (V), and the percentage by which the reading is low. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
True (open-circuit) voltage: $V_{\text{th}} = {Ev}\cdot\dfrac{{R2}}{{R1} + {R2}} =$ **{Vtrue:sig3} V**.

Thévenin resistance seen by the meter: $R_{\text{th}} = \dfrac{({R1})({R2})}{{R1} + {R2}} = {Rth:sig3}$ MΩ.

Reading: $V_{\text{th}}\dfrac{R_V}{R_V + R_{\text{th}}} = {Vtrue:sig3}\cdot\dfrac{{RV}}{{RV} + {Rth:sig3}} =$ **{Vread:sig3} V**, which is **{err:sig3}%** low.

drills.title: Mean free time and drift speed (Drude model)
drills.prompt: For {mat}, use the Drude model to find the mean free time (in femtoseconds, 1 fs = 10⁻¹⁵ s) and the drift speed (in mm/s) when the field inside the metal is {Ef} V/m. Take $m = 9.109\times10^{-31}$ kg and $e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\tau = \dfrac{m}{ne^2\rho}$ with $n = {nn:texsci}$ m⁻³ and $\rho = {rho:texsci}$ Ω·m gives **{tauf:sig3} fs**.

Drift: $v_d = \dfrac{eE\tau}{m} = \dfrac{E}{ne\rho} =$ **{vd:sig3} mm/s**.

drills.title: Platinum resistance thermometer
drills.prompt: A platinum thermometer has $R_0 = 100.0$ Ω at 0 °C and $\alpha = 3.85\times10^{-3}$ per °C. (a) What is its resistance at {T1} °C (3 significant figures)? (b) It later reads {R2:dp2} Ω. What is the temperature, to the nearest degree?

drills.title: Resistivity of doped silicon
drills.prompt: Silicon is doped with ${Nd}\times10^{{pw}}$ donor atoms per m³, each freeing one electron; take the electron mobility as {mu} m²/(V·s) and ignore the few carriers of pure silicon. Find the resistivity (Ω·m) and the resistance (Ω) of a bar {Lmm} mm long with a 1.0 mm² cross-section. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\sigma = ne\mu = ({Nd}\times10^{{pw}})(1.602\times10^{-19})({mu}) = {sig:sig3}$ (Ω·m)⁻¹, so $\rho = 1/\sigma =$ **{rho:sig3} Ω·m**.

$R = \rho\dfrac{L}{A} = {rho:sig3}\times\dfrac{{Lmm}\times10^{-3}}{1.0\times10^{-6}} =$ **{R:sig3} Ω**.
